from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Epidemics are modeled by three population states.",
            "Susceptible (S) are healthy individuals.",
            "Infectious (I) are currently carrying the virus.",
            "Recovered (R) have gained immunity.",
            "Total population N equals S plus I plus R."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Defining Populations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        s_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.6)
        s_text = Text("S", font_size=24).move_to(s_node.get_center())
        s_group = VGroup(s_node, s_text)
        
        i_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.6)
        i_text = Text("I", font_size=24).move_to(i_node.get_center())
        i_group = VGroup(i_node, i_text)
        
        r_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00CED1", fill_opacity=0.6)
        r_text = Text("R", font_size=24).move_to(r_node.get_center())
        r_group = VGroup(r_node, r_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(s_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(s_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(i_group, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(i_group))
        
        arrow_si = Arrow(s_group.get_right(), i_group.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow_si))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(r_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(r_group))
        
        arrow_ir = Arrow(i_group.get_bottom(), r_group.get_top(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow_ir))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        n_text = MathTex("N = S + I + R", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(n_text, 'E5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(n_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Dynamics of Transmission", [

            "Infection happens through contact between Susceptible and Infectious.",
            "Higher beta means faster disease spread."

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Recovery Mechanism (The Gamma Factor)", [
            "Gamma represents the rate of recovery.",
            "Infected individuals transition to the Recovered state.",
            "The infectious period ends as Gamma takes effect."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        gamma_text = Text("Gamma (γ)", color="#00CED1", font_size=32)

        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE).set_length(1.5)
        
        transition_group = VGroup(infected_circle, arrow, recovered_circle).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(transition_group, "D3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"), Write(gamma_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"), FadeIn(transition_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))

            infected_circle.animate.set_color(GREEN),

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Curves", [
            "The SIR model plots state changes over time.",
            "The Infectious curve peaks at the epidemic height.",
            "Susceptible population steadily declines over time.",
            "Recovered population grows as individuals gain immunity.",
            "The curves illustrate herd immunity evolution."
        ])

        # Define Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 2],
            y_range=[0, 100, 20],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        # Place axes in right grid area
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.add(axes)

        # Functions for curves
        s_func = lambda t: 100 * np.exp(-0.4 * t)
        i_func = lambda t: 50 * t * np.exp(-0.4 * t)
        r_func = lambda t: 100 - s_func(t) - i_func(t)

        s_curve = axes.plot(s_func, color="#FFD700", x_range=[0, 10])
        i_curve = axes.plot(i_func, color="#FF4500", x_range=[0, 10])
        r_curve = axes.plot(r_func, color="#00FF00", x_range=[0, 10])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(Create(i_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(s_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(r_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Power of Intervention", [
            "Interventions like distancing reduce beta.",
            "Lowering transmission rates flattens the infectious curve.",
            "Models guide critical public health policies."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve_orig = axes.plot(lambda x: 4 * np.exp(-(x - 3)**2 / 2), color=RED)
        curve_new = axes.plot(lambda x: 2.5 * np.exp(-(x - 3)**2 / 2), color="#32CD32")
        barrier = Line(start=UP*1, end=DOWN*1, color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6)
        
        # Setup visuals in area
        area_group = VGroup(axes, curve_orig, curve_new, barrier)
        self.place_in_area(area_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(barrier))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.play(Transform(curve_orig, curve_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics
outline.target_audience: University students (Introductory Epidemiology or System Dynamics)

sections.title: The Core Concept: Defining Populations
sections.content: Introduce the three compartmental states: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R). Explain the total population constraint (N = S + I + R) and the concept of 'flow' between states.
sections.example: Visualize a group of 100 forest rabbits. Blue (S) are healthy, Red (I) are sick, and Green (R) have developed immunity.

sections.title: The Dynamics of Transmission (The Math of Interaction)
sections.content: Explain the transition rates. Focus on the transmission rate (beta) as the likelihood of infection during contact. Use a graphic representing 'Blue' colliding with 'Red' to become 'Red'.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Red' rabbit hopping through a field; every time it bumps into a 'Blue' rabbit, there is a probability that the 'Blue' rabbit turns 'Red'.

sections.title: The Recovery Mechanism (The Gamma Factor)
sections.content: Introduce the removal rate (gamma), representing the time it takes for an infected individual to stop being infectious (recovery or death). Explain how I decreases while R increases.
sections.example: A timer icon appearing over 'Red' rabbits. Once the timer ends, they shift color to Green, signifying they can no longer infect or be infected.

sections.title: Visualizing the Curves
sections.content: Synthesize the logic into the classic SIR line graph. Discuss the peak of the 'I' curve and what it represents (the epidemic peak). Explain why the 'S' curve always declines and the 'R' curve always rises.
sections.example: An animated line chart evolving in real-time alongside the rabbit simulation: watch the Red curve spike as the forest gets infected and flatten as herd immunity (the Green population) grows.

sections.title: Application: The Power of Intervention
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate how changing variables (e.g., social distancing reducing beta) shifts the curves. Conclude with why mathematical modeling is crucial for public health policy.
sections.example: Show a 'Fence' barrier appearing in the forest animation, reducing the collision frequency between rabbits, resulting in a 'flattened' Red curve on the graph.
